title: Rotate Right
statement: Implement `solve(items, k)`. Return the list rotated right by `k` positions. `k` may be larger than the length. Reduce it modulo the length. An empty list returns an empty list. Rotation by a multiple of the length returns a copy of the same order.
constraints: Right rotation moves the tail to the front
hints: If the list is empty, return an empty list before the modulo.
k %= len(items). A zero k returns a copy.
The new list is items[-k:] + items[:-k]. Reversals are an equivalent in-place method.

approaches.name: Direct
approaches.explanation: Right rotation by k makes the last k elements the new prefix.

editorial: Right rotation by k makes the last k elements the new prefix. Modulo avoids walking k when k is a large multiple of the length. Three reversals do the same rotation with constant extra memory. Either way the order of the two slices stays intact.
